annotations.annotation_text: Fall/resurrection motif "wall" on page 124 ("The Letter from the Midden"): Tim Finnegan tumbling from his ladder, Humpty Dumpty shattering from the wall, Adam falling in Eden — all converge within Biddy Doran the Hen scratching up the mysterious letter from the dump, the Book of Kells as model for textual exegesis. The comic-cosmic Fall during the Age of Gods phase demands its counterpart: resurrection through the whiskey-splash of the water of life (uisce beatha).
sources: The Ballad of Tim Finnegan's Wake. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finnegan%27s_Wake
Atherton, James S. The Books at the Wake. https://archive.org/details/booksatwake0000athe
Opie, Iona and Peter. The Oxford Dictionary of Nursery Rhymes. https://archive.org/details/oxforddictionary0000unse_m4u1

annotations.annotation_text: The Letter motif "letter" on page 124 ("The Letter from the Midden"): ALP's mysterious document — scratched from the midden by Biddy Doran the Hen — represents the genesis of all writing within Biddy Doran the Hen scratching up the mysterious letter from the dump, the Book of Kells as model for textual exegesis. During this Age of Gods phase, the letter functions simultaneously as archaeological artifact, love note, legal deposition, and the text of Finnegans Wake itself.
sources: Bishop, John. Joyce's Book of the Dark. https://archive.org/details/joycesbookofdark0000bish
Deane, Vincent, et al. The Finnegans Wake Notebooks at Buffalo. https://www.brepols.net
